data.long_meaning: Agatha is derived from the Greek word agathos, which means good or kind. historical_references.reference: Saint Agatha was a virgin and martyr venerated in the Catholic Church. She was born in Sicily in the late 3rd century and was subjected to various forms of torture for refusing to marry a pagan official and give in to his advances. She is considered the patron saint of breastfeeding women, bakers, and those suffering from fever and earthquakes.

The Roman martyr Agatha is commemorated in the Eastern Orthodox Church on February 5 and in the Roman Catholic Church on February 5 or on February 15, depending on the local tradition. Her relics are kept in various locations, most notably in Palermo, Sicily.
